name: walk-the-dog
title: Back to the Dog: Buster
kicker: Resilience, tested · back to the dog
html:
Back to the Dog: Buster

A Russell terrier who chews remotes, bites ankles and jumps on everything. So I named a program after him.

Buster: a Chaos Filter for HEART

It sits in front of a server and tampers with its answers on purpose. Each plugin breaks one rule of the spec and says what ARTIE must do about it.

Every Mutation Judged

Pass or FAIL, from ARTIE’s next requests. Seeded, so any failure replays exactly. Nothing corrupted is ever cached.

He tests ARTIE’s resilience, just as he tests mine.

Basically Unstoppable Saboteur Terrierizing Every Representation
Buster doesARTIE must
Forges the ETagrevalidate, or take the 412 and re-sync
Flips one letter in a formrefuse the bytes, fetch them again
Drops an affordancenever act on it
Strips the forms integritynever follow that link
Lies about the rungtreat it as L0, no forms

Five of the eight plugins in the HEART pack.
say: And one more, named after the dog. Buster is a Russell terrier who chews remotes, bites ankles, and jumps on everything. Fitting, given how much of this was built through /remote-control. So I named a chaos filter after him. Buster sits in front of a server and tampers with its answers on purpose: forges a version tag, flips a letter in a form, drops an offered act, lies about how the forms are delivered. Each plugin breaks one rule of the HEART spec and says what ARTIE must do about it; every mutation ends as a pass or a FAIL, seeded, so any failure replays exactly. I can't watch ARTIE every minute either, so something else does. Buster tests ARTIE's resilience, just as he tests mine.

deck:ref.name: no-time
deck:ref.label: NO-TIME
deck:ref.title: No time to type
deck:ref.summary: Family and a new dog took the typing time: one hand on a leash, a phone in the other. Half the fix is Claude Code's /remote-control: the session runs on my machine, steered mostly by speech-to-text dictation. The other half is rigour without watching: the agent must behave the same way every time and follow BDD strictly (Gherkin, red, code, green, commit), so hooks enforce the order and log every run, and the record is read later instead of the agent being monitored. Controls that hold while nobody watches: what this talk asks of agents calling APIs too.

deck:ref.name: artie
deck:ref.label: ARTIE
deck:ref.title: ARTIE: the generic client
deck:ref.summary: Autonomous Restful Traversal and Interactive Engine. Coupled to HEART and HTTP, and to nothing about any one API, as a browser is to HTML. It enters by a bookmark, checks a kept script's pins against what is offered, sends each act with its If-Match validator, and caches forms and schemas (L2).
